overview: Most candidates attempted all MCQs and performance improved across Section A; mechanics was a relative strength.
Good answers selected formulae correctly from the data booklet and set out clear substitution with appropriate s.f. and units.
When a question refers to a figure or graph, its data must be used in the answer - many lost marks by ignoring the given graphs.
Keep full calculator values; mid-calculation rounding caused errors and wrong s.f.
Use precise scientific vocabulary (e.g. do not say 'stress' or 'strain' when 'force' is meant).
The photoelectric effect (especially the gold-leaf electroscope) and percentage difference from an accepted value were weak areas.
assessment_for_learning: Newton's third law pairs: equal size, opposite direction, same type of force, acting on different bodies.
Compressing a spring increases its elastic potential energy store; work is done in the direction of displacement.
Use the Practical Skills Handbook for practical techniques, terminology and the method for percentage difference between calculated and accepted values.
Underline or circle key data in the question.
